paper.title_en: Clouds as near-horizon backgrounds in the radio detection of air showers
paper.abstract_en: Stand-alone radio detection of air showers from cosmic rays or neutrinos relies on effective and efficient suppression of human-made noise sources. We propose here that reflections of human- made transmitters on clouds or other atmospheric phenomena, can cause confusion backgrounds that have not been studied previously. Given the absence of prior modelling, we have developed a simplified model for the reflection strength of clouds in the MHz regime. The results indicate that such reflections are, in principle, detectable, in particular in extremely horizontal geometries with typical experimental set-ups.
